_method: Expected outcomes were established by hand, by a human reading the actual supplied policy wording (USGIC-CSCIndividualHealthInsurance_2017-2018.pdf) against each case's facts -- the same way a reviewer/auditor would validate the system's output. They are not derived from the system under test. Where the policy text is genuinely ambiguous or silent, the expected outcome is NEEDS_REVIEW rather than a guessed determinate answer, consistent with the assignment's abstention requirement.

PUB-001.rationale: Network hospital, appendicitis is not a named 1st-year-waiting-period disease, 14 months continuous coverage exempts the 30-day initial waiting period. Room (INR 30,000) exceeds the 1% Sum Insured cap (INR 5,000) and ambulance (INR 1,200) exceeds its INR 1,000 cap; other categories are within their sub-limits.

PUB-002.rationale: 0 months continuous coverage, 0 prior-insurer years, claim 20 days after inception -- squarely inside the 30-day initial waiting period with no continuity exception, and viral fever is not an emergency-accident scenario carved out elsewhere in the supplied text.

PUB-003.rationale: Treatment is explicitly for a pre-existing condition; only 27 months of continuous coverage have elapsed against the Policy's 48-month pre-existing-disease waiting period, with no portability credit (0 prior-insurer years).

PUB-004.rationale: Domiciliary Treatment definition is satisfied (room unavailable). Domiciliary expenses claimed (doctor + medicines = INR 105,000) exceed the 20% aggregate sub-limit (20% of INR 500,000 = INR 100,000), so INR 100,000 is payable.

PUB-005.rationale: Cataract/eye surgery is one of the Policy's named day-care procedures exempt from the 24-hour minimum stay; 29 months continuous coverage clears the 1st-year specified-disease waiting period regardless. All claimed amounts are within their category sub-limits.

PUB-006.rationale: evidence_context leaves hospital_registered and medical_necessity_confirmed both unknown (null) for what is described only as network_provider=true with no corroborating evidence supplied in the case -- the supplied evidence does not let the Hospital-definition / medical-necessity questions be answered safely.

PUB-007.rationale: No waiting-period issues. Category sub-limits materially reduce the payable amount: room capped at 1% of INR 1,000,000 (INR 10,000 vs INR 80,000 claimed), doctor fees capped at 25% (INR 250,000 vs INR 300,000), other expenses capped at 40% (INR 400,000 vs INR 500,000).

PUB-008.rationale: Cosmetic surgery for a 'cosmetic condition' falls squarely within the Policy's explicit cosmetic/aesthetic-treatment exclusion.

PUB-009.rationale: Pre-hospitalisation (30 days) and post-hospitalisation (60 days) timing are exactly within the Policy's windows and same_condition_confirmed is true, so both are fully payable. Room (INR 15,000) exceeds the 1% Sum Insured cap (INR 5,000); everything else is within its sub-limit.

PUB-010.rationale: Only 8 months of continuous coverage under the current policy, but 1 year of continuous prior coverage with another Indian individual health insurer (with database/claim history received) supplies the portability credit that satisfies both the 1st-year named-disease waiting period and reinforces the general continuity exception. Claimed amounts are within their category sub-limits.

PUB-011.rationale: The facility is non-network and the supplied evidence explicitly leaves hospital_registered unknown and hospital_minimum_criteria_documented false -- the case cannot be finally decided because the Policy's Hospital definition cannot be confirmed on the current record, per the task's own framing.

PUB-012.rationale: The treatment is flagged experimental, and the Policy defines 'Unproven/Experimental Treatment' as its own category, but the supplied policy text contains no explicit numbered exclusion clause naming experimental treatment -- concluding NOT_ADMISSIBLE would rest on an inference from definitions rather than a direct exclusion citation, so the safer, evidence-honest call is to abstain.

CUST-001.rationale: Caesarean delivery for pregnancy/childbirth falls within the Policy's explicit pregnancy/childbirth/caesarean-section exclusion clause.

CUST-002.rationale: 77 months of continuous coverage clears the 48-month pre-existing-disease waiting period. Room (INR 4,000), doctor fees, medicines, and pre/post-hospitalisation are all within their respective category sub-limits, so nothing is deducted and the claim is fully payable.

CUST-003.rationale: Injury sustained while intoxicated with alcohol falls within the Policy's exclusion for injury caused by intentional self-injury and use of intoxicating drugs/alcohol.

CUST-004.rationale: No waiting-period issue (31 months continuous coverage) and no exclusion applies. On a smaller INR 300,000 sum insured, the 1% room cap (INR 3,000) is well below the claimed INR 45,000 room expense, and the ambulance flat cap (INR 1,000) is below the claimed INR 2,000 -- both drive material deductions.

CUST-005.rationale: The supplied policy's 30-day initial waiting period clause contains no carve-out for accidental injury -- it applies to all claims unless the continuity exceptions are met. With 0 months continuous coverage and a claim 24 days after inception, the claim is barred by the initial waiting period as written, even though many other Indian health policies do exempt accidents (a fact this system must not import from outside the supplied text).

CUST-006.rationale: Non-network facility with an entirely empty evidence_context (no registration or minimum-criteria evidence of any kind) -- the Hospital definition cannot be confirmed, so the system should abstain rather than assume network-equivalent status.
